staff.name: Kofi
staff.quote: A fade should look as good in week three as it does when you leave.
staff.bio: Opened Fade District in 2014 after eight years on Call Lane. Still cuts five days a week and still checks every neckline before anyone leaves.

staff.name: Danny
staff.quote: Tell me what you do in the morning. That decides the cut, not the photo.
staff.bio: Trained in scissor work first, clippers second. The one to see if you want length on top that still behaves.

staff.name: Ash
staff.quote: Two hot towels, a sharp razor and no rush. That is the whole secret.
staff.bio: Runs the shave chair. If your beard has a mind of its own, Ash will find the shape it actually wants to be.

staff.name: Rio
staff.quote: First cut? We go slow, we chat, and we get the certificate out after.
staff.bio: Patient, quick and very good with nervous first-timers. Saturdays fill up fast, so book ahead.

questions.a: Pay and display on Call Lane, two minutes' walk, or the Kirkgate Market multi-storey, four minutes. When each one charges is on our Plan your visit page.
Yes. There's no step at the door, and one chair lowers for wheelchair users. Mention it when you book and we'll keep it free.

questions.q: Do I need to book, or can I walk in?
questions.a: Both. Walk-ins are welcome all day. Book ahead for Fridays and Saturdays, which fill up by lunchtime.

questions.q: How long does a cut take?
questions.a: Most cuts take 30 to 45 minutes. A skin fade with a beard shape-up is about an hour.
Message us. If you're more than 15 minutes late we may need to move you to the next free slot.

questions.q: Do you cut Afro and textured hair?
questions.a: Every day. Kofi, Ash and Rio cut Afro and textured hair: skin fades, tapers, line-ups, sponge twists and beard work.

questions.q: Can you copy a photo I bring in?
questions.a: Show us on your phone. We'll tell you honestly if it will work with your hair, and what we'd change if not.

questions.q: What age do you cut kids' hair from?
questions.a: From about 18 months. Rio does most first haircuts, takes it slowly, and every first-timer gets a certificate.
Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay and cash. No minimum spend.
Yes, in the shop, for any amount. They're valid for a year.

blocks.heading: How it started
blocks.body:
Kofi opened Fade District in 2014 after eight years cutting on Call Lane. He wanted a shop where nobody was rushed out of the chair, and where every neckline got checked before you left.

Danny joined in 2016, Ash in 2020 and Rio in 2022. Between them they cut every hair type that walks in.

blocks.alt: The inside of the shop: barber chairs in a row under warm lights, mirrors along the wall.
blocks.caption: Four chairs, one waiting bench, no rush.

blocks.heading: How we work
items: Every cut starts with a chat about what you want and what suits you.
We check the back with a mirror before you get up.
Prices are on the wall and on this site. No surprises at the till.
Kids are welcome every day; Rio has the most patience in Leeds.
